summary:
Review of the second-scenario direct check 38aa89590d3b453bb2c47420aa8e7fe0 for unit-claim-timeout-now-attribution, preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Fresh execution ec71e08710e746bbbe6e7268f032377e completed the comparison: the declarative prerequisite matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete are true, and the assertion held as expected — with the transfer privilege set, a voter that already followed node2 granted a vote to the configured candidate node3 (granted true), while the identical request without the flag was rejected (granted false) and the flag did not defeat the membership check (unconfigured candidate, granted false). This is a corroboration of the privilege's mechanism rather than a new violation; the first scenario of the same requirement already carries the violated comparison.

Product contents: the required checker_correspondence item (no_issue_found, empty counterevidence) covering requirement versus predicate, caller duties, identity/correlation, the event-based oracle (exit 0, assertion held), completion, and all disclosed limits; an applicability item; and a re-resolution of the claim-level applicability issue add89d8bab1d42fe9bd4d7c04645bf4b — open again for this artifact because a resolution answers its own lineage — disposing the documentation-versus-handler condition as independent_scope with sources.

Explicitly retained: the scenario assumes the privilege is set (whether an unattributed sender can cause that is the claim's separate open premise, established by the first scenario); no live cluster, leader traffic or timing was exercised, so only the grant decision was measured; and the reading of the LeadershipTransfer documentation in mixed-version clusters remains an open boundary rather than something the claim absorbs.

Run state: four confirmed in-scope violations (batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery, heartbeat fast-path header gate, TimeoutNow sender attribution, snapshot install log-tail alignment), with the TimeoutNow finding now also carrying measured evidence of its consequence; this review, if accepted, would record the second scenario's held comparison alongside it.
